support_jake: FYI just got a support ticket — customer sees 400 on POST /v1/reranks with 'Unexpected end of JSON input'. They say it started after deploying a proxy.

support_jake: Request body they sent (redacted) — looks truncated:
```json
{
  "items": [
    {"id":"1","query":"How to invest?"},
    {"id":"2","query":"Best funds"}
  ],
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"a","text":"Diversified index funds"},
    {"id":"b","text":"High yield savings"}
  ],
  "top_k": 3,
  <-- EOF/truncated
```

maria_devex: Looks like the payload got cut off (note the trailing comma + arrow). Could be chunked transfer/connection close. Which SDK/version are they using?

support_jake: Customer is on our JS SDK 2.3.1 running in node behind nginx. Console shows: `Error: 400 Bad Request - Unexpected end of JSON input`

ingrid_engineer: Could also be client-side streaming or network close. The payload above is missing the closing brace/array. Two likely causes: 1) client closed connection mid-upload (nginx/proxy timeouts), 2) SDK bug that fails to flush buffer on error.

ingrid_engineer: Quick repro and validation steps:
1) save a complete payload to payload.json (no trailing commas)
2) curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/reranks \ \
   -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \ \
   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \
   --data-binary @payload.json

ingrid_engineer: Server-side pre-send checks we recommend:
```js
if (!Array.isArray(body.candidates) || body.candidates.length === 0) throw new Error('candidates required');
if (typeof body.top_k !== 'number') throw new Error('top_k must be number');
if (!Array.isArray(body.items)) throw new Error('items required');
```

maria_devex: FYI there is a known issue in JS SDK 2.3.1 where an EPIPE/network error could result in a truncated chunk being sent; patched in 2.3.4. Please ask the customer to test with plain curl (above) and/or upgrade SDK. Workaround: set `Content-Length` explicitly or retry on network errors.

support_jake: I'll reply to the customer with repro steps, request an nginx error_log and a raw request capture (tcpdump/ngrep) if they can. Also asking them to try curl and to upgrade the SDK. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
